title: Italian olive-oil cake
summary: A moist, golden single-layer cake made with fruity olive oil and orange zest, dairy-free as written.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Oil a 23 cm (9 in) round pan and line the base with parchment.
Whisk the eggs, erythritol and zests with an electric mixer for 3–4 minutes, until thick and pale.
With the mixer on low, pour in the olive oil in a thin stream, then the almond milk and vanilla.
Whisk the almond flour, coconut flour, baking powder and salt together and fold them in until just combined.
Pour into the pan and bake 35–40 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 15 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack. Dust with powdered erythritol before serving.
tips: The oil's flavour comes through, so taste it first: a harsh oil makes a bitter cake.

origin.history: In the olive-growing regions of Italy, olive oil has long stood in for butter in home baking, and simple oil-based cakes flavoured with citrus are made from Liguria to Sicily. There is no single recorded origin; the cake is a family of regional home recipes rather than a named invention. This version is dairy-free as written.
